body.p: There once lived an old woman. She had three sons. In the autumn the sons went to the forest. Having gone off to hunt, they went to hunt. The old woman remained alone. One day she was whiling the day away. "It's the second morning I'm sitting around in the morning. It seems that there is something by the door, something by the door. At one time my tent seemed like it started falling over. My tent is leaning to the side. I looked up to see what it is sticking into the tent. It's making my tent lean to one side, it looks like. Once a devil showed up in the house. A devil, or what was this? He is beating something against the ground. He took a step forward on the other side and sat down on my son's bed. He sat forward a little again. He hurt his knee, his knee, he made ten arrows out of it. He made four (flintstones/matches?). He tore off a piece of the nose and made a vessel for the glue (fish glue). And from the sunny side of the tent he took an eagle's feather (/half a wing?). With this feather he glued, he made [the arrows]. He glued this feather down. Having come up front, he said: "Which one of my sons will have strength?" He asks the old woman like this: "Which one of my sons will have strength?" Having gone out into the street, he went home from here." Then the old woman whiled two or whatever number of days away. Then in the evening my older son returned home. "Child, you know what? As I was sitting in the morning, after you left, in the street there something by the door. At one time my tent started falling over to the side. My tent started leaning over to the side. I had just looked up, it was a tree or whatever, it was pushing my tent to the side. Ah, once something from the street showed up in the tent. A person or whatever it was, smiling, or maybe laughing. Walking forward along that side, he sat down. He sat around enough, cut up his knee, made ten arrows out of it. He twisted off a piece of his nose and stuck the glue container into the ground. (Having leaned over?) from the sunny side, he took an eagle's feather. He glued together the arrows. Having glued them, he said this. "If any of your sons have the strength, he should chase me. If he has no strength, he shouldn't chase me. Having gone into the house, he said this. Her son, having eaten, went to bed. The next morning he got up, and, having dressed, went the way of the devil. He went forward. The old woman whiled away this day. In the evening it got dark, her middle son come home. Her middle son came home and sat down to eat. "Child, do you know something? You left, and the morning of the second day I was sitting like this. At one time it looked like there was something like this at the door. Oh, oh. At one time it looked like my tent started to fall sideways. I just looked up, there was something my tent was leaning on sideways. Then he showed up in the tent. You look, and he is smiling and laughing. Having taken a step to the other side [of the tent], he sat down. He sat a little, having cut his knee, and made ten arrows out of it. Having torn off his nose, he made a glue container. He took an eagle feather from the sunny side of the tent, having taken the feather, he glued the arrows with these [feathers]. "If he can, if one of your sons has the strength, he should chase me. If he doesn't have the strength, he shouldn't chase me." That's what the devil said. What will the son say. What did he say? He spent the night. The next morning he got up, and having dressed, he set out to chase the devil. Then the second time the old woman whiled away the day, when evening came, the youngest son came. Her son, having taken off his shoes and clothes, sat down. "Son, do you know something? The devil was here. The second morning I was sitting and it looked like there is something by the door, it looked like. One time my tent leaned to the side. I just looked up, some was pressing down on my tent. The old devil looked like it showed himself. From the street, having sat on that side of the tent, he cut his knee, and made ten arrows. He tore off his nose, set the glue container down, sticking up. He took that eagle feather from the sunny side of the tent, made arrows with it, and then, having gone out in the street [he said]. "Where are your sons? If any one of your sons has the strength, he should chase me. If he has no strength, he shouldn't follow me." That's what he said". The son has no words, he lay down to sleep. The next morning he got up, ate, and sat. As the devil sat, that's how he sat too. Having cut his knee, the youngest [son] also made ten arrows. Having torn off his nose, he also made a container of glue. Then the second day (on?) the side of the tent, having turned (he sat?). He also took an eagle feather. He glued these [feathers] on the arrows. As that [someone] went out into the street, having taken these ten arrows, then he set out. He left following the way of the devil. Then the son, chasing, left, he is chasing him. Los was walking, the way he was walking, as if he passed a birdÊ¼s [=beastÊ¼s] feather on the snow [=cut open]. Those two brothers walked slowly, at the front, [having dug out the snow,] they spent the night on the ground [=on the sand], the devil seemed to have spent the night on the head of a small bird (/on the antlers of the deer). Then he set out again. My brothers spent again the night in a hole in the snow[=on the sand], then they set out. From here he reached it. (?) The devil, it seems, on the head of a little bird, that's where spent the night, that's where he spent the night again. Then he set out, he set out. One time again they spent the night, again they spent the night in a hole in the snow [=on the sand]. Then he set out. He only reached the devil's tent. Oh, it looks like, how did my brothers reach this? The skis and all the rest is standing like it stood before. Snow has covered everything, there are no tracks in the street, nothing. I just went into the house, two wild beasts like this are tied up there, their eyes and mouths burning like fire. They wanted (?) to catch this man by the elbows (?), almost did. To two [...][BrM:] The first part of the sentence is unclear. a voice said while they were drying (got quiet), then he went into the tent. The old devil is smiling, laughing. The man appeared (?) to be alive (?). The man (?) said this. Then the second time the old devil popped out into the street, he brought in a pike [fish]. He ate all of the thinly sliced raw pike. He eats thinly sliced raw pike. Once the man wanted to (?) drink very much (?). The devil's daughter is gnawing at her finger. Once, probably, it was like: "I'll gnaw at the back of the pike (spinal cord, bones)." You gnawed at the back of the pike, it was like you drank a pitcher of water. He ate the whole pike. Then they spent the night. The next morning he got up, went out into the street, and brought in a piece of the reindeer's shoulder. He cooked the piece of the reindeer's shoulder on and on. Having cooked it, he got the brain bone out for himself and the meat for the boy. He says, he gnaws at this piece of the reindeer brain and plays. Once the boy ... almost threw a log from the house, while (?) sticking out. Oh-oh! Having jumped away from those teeth of mine (?) of the old man and the woman, my brother-in-law's eye was almost poked out(?)?. Then his brother, having run, got it out. He gnaws and gnaws also. He threw it from this side to the other, it stuck in the middle of the forehead of the old devil. He threw it at the grandfather, at the middle of his forehead. The grandfather says: "Oh-oh, I'll work up a sweat, and I'll be warm." That boy said that. "From the roots of my (young/milk)? teeth, my brother-in-law, what for did [you]? almost (poked out)? my eyes, aaaah!" Then (?), having started to run (?), he took the piece of reindeer's bone out. Then, smiling a little, laughing, he ran out into the street. His daughter said that. "That's the cedar top lying there. You'll go out into the street from here, (in the hallway) there is a wooden hammer. My father stuck it in there. You, having taken that hammer, run! Hammer this cedar top with the wooden hammer, hammer it!" Really, he ran out into the street from his wife, his way is there, you can see it(?). Having taken the hammer, he ran in that direction here, he ran to catch up. He came there: "Where is he hiding?" He hammered the cedar top with a wooden hammer, on and on. Then this boy ran off to home, he grabbed the wooden bowl, the pot (bowl, bowl). He hid in the pot. The old devil got into the tent, he hits this, he hits that, he is nowhere to be seen. He hit the bucket, he hit the pot:[BrM:] Another interpretation is also possible and is struck out in the notebook, as well as the translation given: "The copper said, the pot said ..." "We won't tell. The good food that he was eating we eat, we won't tell." Then he hits this in the tent, he hits that - nowhere to be seen, nowhere. He had just looked, the house (the bottom of the house? at the bottom?), he is sitting. Smiling and laughing the devil ran out into the street. He ran out, by the window there is a coffin, he got quiet there. He fell in there downwards onto a stump. You should hit this stump with this hammer a lot, a lot, his head will be carried (and not he himself will be walking). And his head will be carried. Having run out into the street, having taken this hammer, he set out; the window ... He hammered the stump, on and on. The old devil carried himself weakly from there (?) ... he carried himself away weakly also. He ran into the house, the one who took the needle away from the devil's daughter. The old devil ran into the house, he hit the fire, he hits it (fed up). Nowhere to be seen, nowhere. Fed up. The devil's daughter stuck her needle in. "Grandfather, what are you looking for? I'm sitting right here." The old devil is laughing, the old devil is looking downstream. Then he ran into the street, then he jumped out into the street. In the hall, at the door, a stick is sticking out, that's where he hid. Hammer a lot with this hammer, hammer a lot. Then he carried himself up, crying out. Then, having gone out, true, he hammered so much, so much. He carried himself weakly from there, he started laughing as he entered the house. He stands here and there (?), then, it seems, he laughs the second time. He spent the night. Having got up the next morning, he drank tea. He drank some tea, ate, having finished eating, he stood here and there. He ran out into the street, having waited, the man, where did he go. It was quiet. One time he came, he is crunching a piece of bird cherry. Having thought, he said this: "Where did you find the bird cherry? Probably, I would see." He also jumped out into the street. Oh, it looks like he ran that way. The old devil, he went there, he went there too. Oh, just found it - this fire is giving out smoke. He hardly went into the tent, it looks like the devil's grandmother is sitting there. Her head like a swan's feather lying there. Like snow. She just grabbed the hammer in order to cut up this man. She just grabs the hammer. This man, having taken the hammer from the devil woman, slashed out to her face, he killed the devil woman. Then he stuffed bird cherry into the devil's grandmother. [KuAI:] From this moment on the text is translated by Alexander Sargaev.He took the bird cherry and brought it home. He came home, chewing a chunk of the bird cherry.[KuAI:] The phrase is repeated three times. Then the man beat (?) me, the man beat (?) me.[KuAI:] The phrase is repeated two times. That is how they became devils. He spent some time, they went to the devil grandmother's home. Then, just setting out ... The devilish old woman died from the bird cherry pits. Having eaten the bread, she swallowed it. The devil's people just came home, they sat down, crying. He is sitting there like nothing happened. It got dark. When the sky got light, he ran out on the the street. The daughter said that. "Then, when he runs to the street, set up traps by the door. You, when he runs to the street ... Hit him with sticks." Then having gone into the house, like he said, the man beat me. [KuAI:] From this moment on the text is translated by M.V. Sargaeva. The text fragment from sent. 216 to sent. 226 seems to repeat the fragment from sent. 200 to sent. 214, translated by Alexander Sargaev, but very roughly.Then, having come back, he is gnawing at a piece of bird cherry, gnawing a little. Saying, people (?) you.[KuAI:] The phrase is repeated two times. [KuAI:] Meaning: "Why didn't they kill you? That's how the old devil becomes, having waited a little (to the doors)? (from where did they keep you)?. Oh, oh - this hardly went - my mother, having choked on carp gills, died. Having swallowed the spine of the carp, she died. The old devil came home, crying a little, crying a little. It got dark. When it became light, he ran out into the street, he jumped out into the street. His daughter said this. "Having run out into the street, he set up traps. When you go out into the street, start hitting with a stick. All so that you would make a noise (so that the traps would slap shut and make noise)". Then, after the old devil went into the house, he went out into the street. He started hitting all (the traps) with a stick. He make all the devil's traps make noise (closed them all). He went home. Says, man you (?), man you (?) (how did you stay alive?). He started like that. He jumped out for a while, went home. He showed up at the house from the street, the devil's traps have cut him all up (caught). Everybody is standing on his skin. He got home together with the traps. This boy, having run up to him, tore off from his skin (the traps), into the forest he went. Having torn it off, he threw them into the forest. The old devil stood there, here and there. He lies around. Then they spent the night. Having got up the second morning, the old man is sharpening his axe: slash, slash (?). He sharpened the axe. "Here, not too far, there is a birch (from which one can make a cup) lying for food, we'll go up to this birchtree of ours". True, the two of them went to this birchtree. The grandfather cut down (the tree) from above to the shoulder of a sitting person. He cut down the small branches at the bottom. One time he stood like that (he said). "Grandson, let me tie you up with a leash". He tied the granddaughters up with a belt, tied up this boy like this, as if he were a hank of yarn. "Grandson, come on, move!" The grandson just pressed a little, the ropes flew off, all the ropes broke off. "So, grandpa, where will I find the ropes? I have no ropes. I have a thin hair string somewhere." He tangled up the old man with it, with this thin hair string. He tangled the old devil with it: "So, grandpa, press on it!" Los-ira hardly pressed, as if suede (?) is being stretched (?) (similarly stretchy but non-breaking string), he left (?) the old devil. He ran home. He ran home, he went to bed with the devil's daughter. Once[KuAI:] Repeated 8 times. in the middle of the night, in the morning (?) night, [scratching]: scratch, scratch. The one who [pulled out] a birch stump completely, he is swearing [and going] home. It's as if he overturned such thick birch roots. Croak.[KuAI:] Repeated 8 times. He jumped out into the street. And who is this gut old man, what is this gut? Having got up (?) with a knife, he cut it up, having cut it up, he broke it up, he cut it away, broke it up, he took (threw) the strings into the house. The old devil is hardly breathing, took (a piece)? into the house. Perhaps he slept, or perhaps he spent the night. The next morning he got up, the boy is figuring it out: "Father will probably kill us."[KuAI:] Having married the devil's daughter, he now calls the devil his father. His brain is turning/going(?). One time this boy went to the forest. What? This boy left for the forest. Oh. He left, oh. Once still it was as if he stood like that (said). "Probably the devil will catch up (?) with me (?)[OSV:] 2 words are indecipherable..[KuAI:] Repeated 3 times. The old devil is chasing me. Where will I go?" Turning into a black sable, he climbed up a tree. That old devil got angry, he is running back. He says: "And where will a simple man get shamanic wisdom from? Are you helping? And where will a simple man get shamanic wisdom from?" He is swearing at his own daughter. He took two of this boy's animals into his house. The old devil poured grease into the ears of two animals so they couldn't hear him. So they couldn't hear him, he poured this grease in. He asked his daughter this way. "Maybe he'll send the birds to the dogs." This boy ... having killed and torn apart these little birds, chase him out into the street."The father is trying to convince his daughter like this. It's true, I tied this man's animals to the house. This devil then caught an eagle owl.[BrM:] Unclear, what the eagle-owl is doing here. He climbed up the tree ... Once he cut down the tree, he cut down trees in a way. He cuts it quick, he is figuring it out. The other one hardly sent the little bird. The little birds had just left, they burst into the house. This devil's daughter, having hit and torn, he sent us again. "Where will I hide, probably, it's as if the devil eats me."[BrM:] It is unclear, who is saying this. He sent the eagle owl, the eagle owl left, the devil sat on the roof of the house / the smoke opening of the tent. The eagle owl had cried out such that the devil's daughter crawled into a corner (?) of the house, she didn't know where herself. [The daughter] flew off to a corner of the house, having been frightened. Those little birds flew into the house, and they ate all the grease out of the ears of those two animals. The two animals just came to: what is it (?), the devil is about to eat our owner. It's as if even (?) the iron rope started to clink, those two animals ran away, they broke/tore off. Having run, they left, they left. Once I (?). He came, here he came. The larch is about to fall down. He saw, it looks like, those animals of mine showed themselves. He says, face! (making the animals turn on the owner) We'll eat him together. He sends these two animals running there. The two animals arrived, they tore the old devil into two. They finished the old devil, they killed him. Then, having come back, he is swearing at the devil's daughter: why did you try so hard? Once my father asked me like that with words, where can I go? Then having arrived home with the devil's daughter at the mother's house, they are living. This is the end, the end.
